svg.aria-label: Diagram: the three location scopes of Google Cloud resources, showing which resources are global, which regional and which zonal, and the two cross-zone rules that follow
svg.title: Google Cloud location scope: global, regional and zonal resources
svg.text: Every resource has a scope, and it decides what can reach it
A narrower scope can use a wider one. The reverse never holds, and the assignment is not the one most people guess.
Global — reachable from any region or zone
VPC networks · firewalls · images · snapshots · instance templates
global static external IP addresses · Cloud Interconnects
The VPC network being global is the single biggest difference from what most people expect.
One network spans every region. So do your firewall rules.
Regional — reachable only within the same region
subnets · regional static external IP addresses · regional managed
instance groups · regional instance templates · Interconnect attachments
A global network cut into regional subnets. The network spans the world; the address ranges do not.
Zonal — reachable only within the same zone
compute instances · zonal Persistent Disks and Hyperdisks · machine
types · zonal managed instance groups · GPUs · Cloud TPUs
Machine types are zonal too, so the shape you want may not exist in the zone you picked.
An instance cannot attach a disk in another zone
Zonal resources are reachable only from their own zone.
But it can talk to an instance in another zone
Provided both are on the same VPC network, which is global.
